title: [storage] The build output of landed objectives goes: spawn scratch sweep, print-only with a digest, --apply only on the list read (--expect-digest), the in-use proof with exact --excuse pairs, and only the very directories judged removed
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 145 [storage] (after 140; the owner's storage line, lead-mac 02:39, sync/research-storage-layerfs-2026-11-14.md, item 1; projects-47's scope and decisions of 2026-11-14): the build output of landed objectives goes. `spawn scratch sweep` removes only what an owner file (objective 140) names as build output, once its objective has landed and its lease has ended. It is print-only unless --apply is given. It is the one deleter of its kind.

Where things stand.
- Reviewer scratch (/data/tmp/ccd) is 92.0 GB on disk (exp3.py, 02:3x), 57% of the used disk. Of it, 45.7 GB is Rust dependency and object files, and 44.7 GB is incremental build state, mostly in target/ folders of objectives long landed.
- 140 gives each scratch folder an owner file: agent, objective, created and lease, and the folder's build paths, each a relative path ending in `target`. The page lists these folders, whether their objective landed, and their lease. Nothing removes them.
- scripts/maintenance.sh is the one deleter today, for the gate's `spawn-gate.*` scratch. It is not changed here.
- On this host our uid has non-dumpable or sandboxed processes whose /proc cannot be read: the login's (sd-pam), gpg-agent, two python3s, and a running gate's spawn processes. The in-use proof below has to name them, not guess.

Hard limits:
- Nothing is removed but a build path an owner file names. Never the folder itself, its sources, its owner file, logs or proofs.
- No symlink is followed.
- The live database is only read.
- Nothing schedules the sweep: a timer is a later, separately reviewed step.

Required behaviour.
(1) Which folders.
- `spawn scratch sweep [--excuse <pid>:<start ticks>]... [--apply --expect-digest <digest>]` decides from the owner files only, never from scratch.unowned (rev-g's N1 on 140).
- It reads the claimed folders the Core lines' scratch walk finds:
  - the Core lines file's `storage.scratch_roots`;
  - claims at a root's top level or one below;
  - the walk's exclusions and refused roots;
  - a folder holding a .jsonl is never read.
- At sweep time each folder is checked again against the names and places the walk never counts (rev-g's N3), since the walk does not check them one level down: .transcripts, incident-*, *.pending, *-pending, scratch_exclude, and the never-counted places ($HOME, Claude's projects dir, /data/recovery, the backups), each also by its resolved path.
- With no roots it is refused.
- It reads the store's landings once: `spawn_postgres::verifications::CLAIMED_LANDED`, 140's read over the claimed pairs, made only when a folder is claimed. If they cannot be read, or the store cannot be opened, it is refused with "nothing removed" and no URL printed.
(2) A build path goes only when all of these hold:
- its claim's lease has ended;
- the store has a task.landed of its mission and objective. This is the fleet's code landing; a contract landing does not count, as in 140.
- it is a build path by 140's rule: relative, plain parts, last part `target`;
- every component under the folder exists and is a real directory, not a symlink, on the folder's device;
- it holds a CACHEDIR.TAG, a regular file starting with the standard's signature;
- nothing under it is a transcript (*.jsonl) or on another device;
- no process uses it (3).
(3) The in-use proof (/proc).
- No process may have its cwd, root or exe at or under the path, an open file there (fd), or a mapping there (maps). maps is how rustc's proc-macro .so files from target/ show.
- Paths are compared by component (target2 is not under target), with " (deleted)" stripped.
- A definite use is reported ahead of an unknown one, whatever the order of /proc.
- A process of the path's owner whose /proc cannot be read refuses the path ("in use unknown: process <pid> (<comm>) of its owner cannot be read"), with two exceptions:
  - its /proc/<pid>/comm is in the fixed list EXCUSED, today only "(sd-pam)", and it started before the claim was made (/proc/<pid>/stat field 22 plus /proc/stat btime, USER_HZ 100). Each such process is printed on an "excused" line.
  - its exact pair <pid>:<start ticks> was given by --excuse.
- An unknown start refuses.
- Unreadable processes of other users are not counted: their cwd, files and mappings cannot be seen.
(4) Excuses and the digest: the reviewed list is the applied list (projects-47; the redaction tool's real pass has the same shape).
- Every run first lists each unreadable process of the user once, as `unreadable <pid>:<start ticks> <comm>`, or as `excuse <pid>:<start ticks> <comm>` for those --excuse names. The excused set comes first in the output, beside the list.
- --excuse is taken in print-only runs too, so the list a reviewer reads is the one --apply acts on. A pair that is not an unreadable process of the user running now is refused, with nothing removed: a stale pair (pid reused, process gone) is never ignored.
- The print-only list ends with `digest <sha256>`. It covers what would go: each `would-remove` row as printed (path, bytes, owner, the `ids <dev>:<ino>,…` of the folder and of each component down to the build path, and the `claim <sha256>` of the whole claim, its owner file's line, every field), and the --excuse pairs, sorted. So a directory put at the path between the print-only run and --apply, even a tagged one of the same size, or a claim released and made again with the same owner shown, is another row and another digest, and --apply refuses (cc-astra's A64 on R3). The per-path comparisons at --apply (6) stay as well. Equal ids and bytes are not a snapshot of a directory's contents: a writer inside the judged directory is still not excluded (the premise in (6)).
- --apply requires --expect-digest, and --expect-digest requires --apply. --apply recomputes the list and its digest. When the digest differs ("the list is not the one read (its digest is now …); nothing removed"), it is refused and nothing is removed. It still judges each path again just before removal (6).
- The reader of the print-only list decides each excuse at run time. A gate's sandboxed processes are never excused: the lead runs --apply when no gate is running.
(5) The list, one line per build path, tab-separated:
- `would-remove <path> <bytes> <agent> <mission>/<NNN> ids <dev>:<ino>,… claim <sha256>` (print only), or `removed …` (with --apply);
- `stays <path> <agent> <mission>/<NNN>: <why>`. The why is one of "lease runs", "not landed", "not a build path", "<component> is a symlink", "is not a directory", "is on another device", "no CACHEDIR.TAG", "<file> is a transcript", "in use: process <pid>'s cwd|root|exe|open file|mapping", "in use unknown: …", "not there", "its claim changed", "its path changed" or "changed since the list";
- `excused <path> process <pid> <comm>: cannot be read, started before the claim`;
- then "would remove (print only; nothing removed) <n> build path(s), <bytes> bytes", or "removed <n> build path(s), <bytes> bytes".
(6) With --apply, each path is judged again just before it goes:
- its owner file must still hold the very claim listed (every field, rev-g's n1 on R1: a release and a new claim are a change, "its claim changed"), with its lease ended;
- every rule of (2) and (3) must still hold.
- the row approved is the row removed (cc-astra's A59 on R2): the re-judged size and the re-judged (dev, ino) of the folder and every component must equal the listed ones. Otherwise the path "stays … changed since the list".
Then what is removed is the very directory judged (rev-g's F1 on R1, cc-astra's A58 on R2), from file descriptors and never from a name resolved again:
- The judge records the (dev, ino) of the folder and of each component.
- The removal opens the folder, then each component through the one before, then the build path's directory itself, each with rustix's `openat(…, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC)`. Each must fstat as the one judged.
- The directory's contents are removed from its own fd:
  - a file or symlink is `unlinkat`ed (the link itself, never what it names);
  - a directory is `openat`ed through it (no symlink followed), must fstat as the entry just read, is emptied the same way, and is then removed with `unlinkat(…, AT_REMOVEDIR)`, which takes only an empty directory.
  - an entry named *.jsonl (a transcript), or on another device than the build path's directory, is never removed or entered (rev-g on R2): the removal stops there, "failed … is a transcript: it is never removed" or "… is on another device", and what is left stays under the judged name.
- Last, the emptied directory's name is removed from its pinned parent with `AT_REMOVEDIR`, only while that name still lstats as the judged directory. A directory put at that name since (another real one, with anything in it) is never emptied or removed. If the name no longer holds the judged directory, the run reports "failed … its contents were removed, but its name no longer holds it: the empty directory is left".
- Anything changed before the build path's directory is opened stays, "its path changed", and nothing is removed.
- No working directory is changed, and no name is renamed, so there is no crash leftover: a run killed part way leaves the judged directory under its own name, partly emptied. The next print-only lists it again by the same rules, since its claim and landing are unchanged.
- A removal that fails is printed "failed" and the sweep exits 1; it exits 0 otherwise.
- What it relies on, and what it does not promise: a claim's lease is no lock the system enforces. The sweep relies on the lease having ended (the owner's word that the build output is no longer needed) and on no process using the path when it is judged again. A process that starts writing there after that judgement, against an ended lease, is not stopped: what it writes inside the judged directory goes with it. Nothing outside that directory is ever reached.
(7) 140's owner file write uses create_new for its temporary file (rev-g's N2), so a symlink or file at that name is never followed or overwritten.

The deleter's answers:
- Reach: only `<claimed folder>/<build path>`, and only the very directories judged: each component is pinned by (dev, ino) from the folder down, and the removal works from the judged directory's own fd (6).
  - The folder comes from the page's walk, which never goes through a symlink, and is rechecked against every exclusion at sweep time.
  - The build path is relative, made of plain parts and ends in target, checked in 140 and again here.
  - Each component is lstat'd, on the folder's device.
- In-use proof: (3), and (4) for --excuse: only exact pairs of running unreadable processes, printed first.
- Scope: never a folder without an owner file, never a path the owner file does not name, never the folder itself.
- Print-only first: without --apply nothing is removed. --apply acts only on the list read: its digest must match.
- Who runs it: the lead runs the first --apply on this host, after rev-g reads the print-only list of a live run. The lead is the only one who runs a deleter, and decides each --excuse from that list. cc-astra re-checks before the PASS counts.
- Tests: those that remove run in scratch dirs of their own, never under the real home (the unit tests refuse one under $HOME). 145.sh runs under a scratch HOME.

What stays as it is: 140's claim, renew and release (but (7)); the page and its figures; the walk; maintenance.sh; every other command.

Tests (unit):
- crates/spawn-cli/src/scratch_sweep.rs:
  - each rule alone keeps its path: no tag, a .jsonl, through a symlink, a file named target, not there, not a build path, in use;
  - only a landed claim with an ended lease goes, and print only removes nothing;
  - removal keeps the sources and the owner file;
  - a claim changed between list and removal stays: renewed, gone, or released and made again;
  - rev-g's swap test (kept as written): a component swapped for a symlink to a target outside, while the --apply re-judgement's in-use proof runs, removes nothing outside, and the path "stays … its path changed";
  - cc-astra's A58: the build path's directory replaced by another real one, holding a sentinel and a .jsonl, right after the judged directory is opened and checked (a barrier inside the removal). Nothing in the replacement is removed, and the run reports the name no longer holds the judged directory. The same replacement after the re-judgement's checks, through the sweep: "its path changed", with the sentinel kept;
  - cc-astra's A59: the path grown between --apply's digest check and its re-judgement stays "changed since the list", and the new file is kept;
  - rev-g's A59 test (kept as written, rg_bytes_added_after_the_digest_keep_the_path): bytes added after the apply-time list was counted and before the re-judgement keep the path, "stays";
  - a transcript put inside the judged directory after its judgement (a barrier inside the removal) is never removed, and the run says why;
  - excused processes are printed;
  - the in-use proof on a /proc of the test's own:
    - cwd, and a mapping with " (deleted)";
    - a near name that is not under the path;
    - an unreadable process: listed and started before is excused; started since is refused; not listed and started before is refused; an unknown start is refused;
    - an exact --excuse pair passes, and another start does not;
    - a definite use is named ahead of an unknown one;
    - the unreadable listing, of this uid only;
  - the real /proc: nothing uses a fresh dir (every unreadable process of ours excused), and this process's open file does;
  - the digest: of what would go (each row: path, bytes, owner, directory ids, claim sha256) and the excuses, not of what stays;
  - cc-astra's A64: between two separate runs, another tagged directory of the same size put at the path, then (put back) the claim made again with the same owner shown: --apply with the first digest is refused both times, and nothing is removed;
  - --apply with a digest not of the list is refused, and nothing is removed;
  - the arguments: --apply and --expect-digest only together; --excuse only as <pid>:<ticks>, in either mode.
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/scratch.rs: a folder the walk never counts is never swept.

Dependency: rustix 1.1.6 (already in the lock through spawn-host; the workspace's `rustix = { version = "1", features = ["fs", "process"] }`) gains a direct edge from spawn-cli: `rustix.workspace = true` in crates/spawn-cli/Cargo.toml. Cargo.lock's one changed line is `+ "rustix",` in spawn-cli's dependencies. No new crate.
Files: crates/spawn-cli/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/spawn-cli/src/scratch_sweep.rs (new); crates/spawn-cli/src/scratch_owner.rs (the verb, its usage, create_new); crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (the module, MORE_USAGE); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs (claimed_scratch: the page's walk with a sweep's bound, rechecked); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/scratch.rs (sweepable). No other open objective touches them except 140, this objective's base.
Size: over the 300-line rule by projects-47's exception. It was granted at about 395 lines, and reconfirmed at about 540 after --excuse, the unreadable listing and the sweep-time recheck were added. The digest followed at the lead's request, then R2's pinned removal and whole-claim check (rev-g's F1 and n1), R3's removal from file descriptors (cc-astra's A58 and A59, rev-g on R2), and R4's directory ids and claim sha256 in the rows and the digest (cc-astra's A64). This is the size as published. A split would ship either a judge with no command, or a command with no in-use proof.
- Code and doc comments: +779 −4.
  - scratch_sweep.rs: 719.
  - core_lines.rs: +32.
  - scratch.rs: +12 −1.
  - scratch_owner.rs: +14 −2.
  - main.rs: +2 −1.
- Tests: +744 (scratch_sweep.rs 723, scratch.rs 21).
- Cargo.toml +3, Cargo.lock +1.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/145.sh, black box, with SPAWN_BIN and a test database of its own, under a scratch HOME.
- It seeds objectives 1/7 and 1/9 as landed and 1/8 as not.
- Through the binary it claims and releases eleven folders. Each breaks one rule, except two: one at the top level and one a level below.
- It holds two of them with a process (a cwd, an open file).
- It makes one build path a symlink after its claim.
It checks:
(1) print only: every line as (5) says, then the total and the digest; nothing under the scratch root or outside it changes. Where this host has unreadable processes, the two eligible paths stay "in use unknown". Each unreadable process is named by its pair.
(2) without the landings (a database that is not there) it is refused: it says "nothing removed", prints no URL, and nothing changes.
(4) refused, with nothing changed: --apply without --expect-digest; --apply with a digest that is not the list's; an excuse whose pair names no unreadable process.
(3) the list read with every unreadable pair excused would remove exactly the two build paths. --apply with those excuses and that list's digest prints the excused set first. It removes exactly the two build paths, prints them and the total, and leaves everything else as it was: the symlink's target outside, the incident-9 folder one level down, and the folder holding a .jsonl.
On the base (live main 22d0fdde with 140's throwaway, f45cd98d), 145.sh exits 1, with 22 checks failed. The first is "(1) the print-only sweep exits 0 (spawn: usage: spawn scratch claim …)": the base has no sweep.

Proof (rev-e-96, sync/obj-145/145-proof.txt; R4 s145b obj145-live 2bd37a8d on R3 37c55942, on f45cd98d = live main 22d0fdde + 140's throwaway; run-r4.sh's output s145out11, with 145.sh as published):
- 145.sh: the base exits 1 (22 checks, (3)'s retries included). The throwaway exits 0 twice, and 140.sh and 094.sh still pass. R3's proof (r3/145-proof.txt): 4 of 5 then 3 of 3; the one failure was an excused process ending before --apply, which 145.sh now retries.
- --list for spawn-cli and spawn-postgres against the base: 0 missing, 15 new tests only.
- clippy -D warnings is clean (spawn-cli, spawn-postgres, all targets), and `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. The unit tests pass (scratch_sweep, scratch_owner, core_lines: 70).
- Host note:
  - This host has 7 to 10 unreadable processes of this user at any time (the login's (sd-pam), gpg-agent, two python3s, and running gates' spawn).
  - 145.sh's (3) tries a round again, at most three times, when a new unreadable process appeared, --apply found the list changed, or an excused process ended before --apply. Each of these is the sweep refusing, with nothing removed. Only a clean round is judged.
- Thirty-one mutants (mut-145.py), each applied alone. Thirty are killed:
  - by 145.sh and a unit test: apply-without-digest, cwd-ignored, digest-unchecked, excused-any-comm, fd-ignored, landed-ignored, lease-ignored, print-only-removes, symlink-followed, tag-ignored, unknown-first, unreadable-ignored;
  - by 145.sh only: excuse-unchecked, store-error-ignored, sweepable-ignored;
  - by a unit test only: claim-fields-only (the re-claim test), digest-omits-claim and digest-omits-ids (A64's test), digest-omits-excuses, empty-by-name (A58's test and the transcript test), excuse-any-start, excused-any-time, excused-unnamed, fd-jsonl-ignored (the transcript test), jsonl-ignored, maps-ignored, no-rejudge, remove-by-full-path (rev-g's swap test and A58's), row-not-kept (A59's test and rev-g's rg_bytes test), under-by-text.
  - fd-dev-ignored survives: the removal's own check for another device. Nothing in a test can put a mount inside a judged directory without mount rights. The judgement already refuses another device anywhere under the path (size(); that check has no test either, for the same reason), so this check only matters for a mount made between the judgement and the removal.
  - Why the scenario cannot catch the unit-only ones:
    - On this host every eligible path stays "in use unknown" until it is excused, so print-only sweeps here never show (sd-pam) excusing alone.
    - The walk never lists a folder holding a .jsonl.
    - No scenario process maps a file.
    - A swap, a re-claim, growth or a transcript inside one sweep needs a hook between its judgement and its removal, which only a unit test has.

Verified by:
- The sessions claim their folders (140).
- The lead runs `spawn scratch sweep --excuse …` (print only) on this host while no gate runs, with the excuses decided from a first plain list. rev-g reads that list and its digest.
- The lead runs `spawn scratch sweep --apply --excuse … --expect-digest <that digest>` once. cc-astra re-checks.
- The day after, exp3.py's reviewer scratch is under 40 GB (from 92 GB), and free disk is read too. The lead posts both in sync.
